title: geometry.partition refuses a body with a revolved ring groove for planes parallel to the groove's axis (kernel nudge), though SolidCraft cuts the same half cleanly
body:
### Observed failure

`geometry.partition` refuses a block that has a revolved ring groove (an undercut at the floor of a counterbore) for every datum plane **parallel** to the groove's axis:

```
partition `H`: the kernel could not cut `Block` (the operation failed: the cut is only made off the plane (SolidCraft's kernel: Boolean retry: tool displacement 5.435255e-4 mm, rotation 2.000000e-6 rad); the plane runs along a face or edge of the body: move it off (by a fraction of the element size))
```

The plane doesn't run along any face or edge, and moving it doesn't help. On a larger body, offsets from 0.0001 mm to 20 mm on either side all failed with the same nudge displacement. A plane **square** to the axis partitions fine. The same block without the groove partitions on every plane.

SolidCraft 0.18.2, the kernel version FieldCraft pins, intersects the same block with a half-space box at x = 0.3 cleanly: no retry, with boxes 100, 2,000 and 20,000 mm across. So the failure looks specific to how the partition builds or applies its cut, not to the geometry.

**Effect:** a half model with symmetry can't be made in FieldCraft from a design that has revolved relief grooves at its bearing seats. The workaround is to cut the half in SolidCraft first, which loses the link to the source design.

### Reproduction

1. Build the design with SolidCraft (0.18.2 here): `solidcraft-cli run groove.json --save groove.solidcraft`. It is a 60 × 30 × 60 block, a Ø30 counterbore 7.8 deep along Y, a Ø14 through hole, and one revolved R1.5 groove at the counterbore's floor corner:

```json
{"commands":[
 {"command":"solid.box","params":{"length":60,"width":30,"height":60,"corner":[-30,0,-30],"body_name":"Block"}},
 {"command":"solid.cylinder","params":{"diameter":30,"height":7.8,"base":[0,-0.01,0],"axis":[0,1,0],"operation":"cut","targets":["Block"]}},
 {"command":"solid.cylinder","params":{"diameter":14,"height":32,"base":[0,-1,0],"axis":[0,1,0],"operation":"cut","targets":["Block"]}},
 {"command":"sketch.create","params":{"plane":"XY","offset":"0"}},
 {"command":"sketch.line","params":{"points":[[16,7.5],[14.5,7.5],[14.5,9]],"infer":false}},
 {"command":"sketch.arc.three_point","params":{"start":[14.5,9],"end":[16,7.5],"through":[17.060660,10.060660]}},
 {"command":"sketch.finish","params":{}},
 {"command":"solid.revolve","params":{"axis":"y","angle":"360 deg","direction":"symmetric","operation":"cut","targets":["Block"]}}
]}
```

2. Partition it with FieldCraft: `fieldcraft-cli run plan.json`:

```json
[
 {"command": "geometry.open", "params": {"path": "groove.solidcraft"}},
 {"command": "geometry.datum", "params": {"name": "D", "by": {"type": "offset", "plane": "yz", "offset": 0.3}}},
 {"command": "geometry.partition", "params": {"name": "H", "datum": "D", "bodies": ["Block"]}}
]
```

| Datum plane | With the groove | Without the groove (the same script minus the sketch and revolve) |
|---|---|---|
| `yz` at 0.3 (parallel to the axis) | refused, as above | partitions |
| `xy` at −10 (parallel to the axis) | refused, as above | partitions |
| `zx` at 20 (square to the axis) | partitions | partitions |

A one-sided revolve fails the same way as the symmetric one.

### Investigation

- `partition.rs` `halves()` refuses any cut that needed the kernel's tool nudge (#427), so the refusal itself is deliberate. What isn't expected is that the cut needs the nudge at all.
- A plain SolidCraft `solid.box … operation: intersect` with the same half-space succeeds without any retry, as described above.

### Version and platform

FieldCraft develop 8b1a01e (`fieldcraft-cli` 0.7.0, built from source) on Windows 11. The same failure was seen on develop b2b3500 on Linux x86_64 with a larger body. The designs were saved by SolidCraft 0.18.2.
